changes: Date: resolved the chronogram 'śaranavācarake' as śara (5), nava (9), acara/acala (7). Read right to left this gives 795. Year field set to 795 with a query.
Date: era left as unspecified, but ce_approx set to 1675 (if NS 795). A three-digit year in a Newari-script manuscript points to Nepāla Saṃvat.
Date: tithi narrowed to tṛtīyā. Gaurī/Girijā's tithi is the 3rd (cf. Gaurītṛtīyā), so Vaiśākha śukla 3 is Akṣayatṛtīyā. The 8th is less likely.
Purpose rephrased: copied for the good of people (pravaralokahitam); it is not a merit-transfer formula.
Notes: added that the title in the colophon differs from the one in the verse.

date.as_written: abde gate śaranavācarake (!) vicitraṃ, vaiśākhamāsi dhavale girijātithau tat | vāre ravau
date.year: 795 (śara-nava-acara, read right to left; reading uncertain)

notes: The chronogram 'śaranavācarake (!)' is corrupt. Best reading: śara = 5, nava = 9, acara (= acala, 'immovable', i.e. the mountains) = 7. Read right to left this gives 795. The era is not named. In a Newari-script manuscript NS is most likely, which gives c. 1675 CE; if the year were VS 795 or ŚS 795 the date would be implausible. Girijātithi is taken as tṛtīyā (Gaurī's tithi), so Vaiśākha śukla 3 is Akṣayatṛtīyā. The verse is metrically loose. The colophon names the work Svaratattvodaya, while the scribe's verse calls it svaratattvabodhaka; the catalogue title follows the verse. The scribe Gaṇapati matches the catalogue field.
